## Requirement it fulfilled
# Substrate requirement: quantitative simultaneous congruence stability

## Goal
Formalize a paper-independent quantitative stability theorem for finite-dimensional real square matrices under approximate simultaneous congruence diagonalization, together with the compactness/continuity exclusion lemma that yields a positive non-effective radius outside a normalized local chart.

## Provides (API contract)
- A reusable definition of the simultaneous-congruence residual for a finite family of real square matrices and diagonal shift vectors.
- A reusable affine determinant/minor separation predicate for the shift-vector family.
- A theorem giving an explicit linear operator-norm bound between an exact normalized reference matrix and an approximately feasible normalized candidate. The modulus must expose its dependence on dimension, affine separation, covariance/shift scale, and reference/candidate condition-number bounds.
- A compactness/continuity theorem giving a strictly positive minimum residual on the normalized candidates outside a prescribed local chart, hence an existential positive exclusion radius.

## Statement / milestones
For a finite nonempty family of real `d × d` matrices, an exact reference `B₀`, and a candidate `B`, assume unit-diagonal (or an equivalently explicit scale-fixing) normalization, exact simultaneous congruence diagonalization at `B₀`, approximate feasibility at `B`, a positive affine-minor separation margin for the associated diagonal shift vectors, uniform operator-norm scale bounds, and operator-norm condition-number bounds for both matrices. When all covariance congruence residuals are at most `ε` and `ε` is below an explicit admissible threshold, prove `‖B - B₀‖op ≤ C ε`, with `C` expressed from `d`, the separation margin, scale bounds, and condition bounds.

Separately, for a compact normalized candidate set and a continuous nonnegative residual that vanishes only at the reference inside the relevant exact-identification class, prove that the residual has a positive attained minimum on candidates outside a specified open/local neighborhood of the reference. Package the resulting positive non-effective exclusion radius without claiming computability.

The API may choose equivalent finite-dimensional matrix norms if it supplies explicit comparison constants sufficient to recover the operator-norm conclusion.

## Standard reference
Standard finite-dimensional perturbation analysis: continuity and compact extreme-value arguments for isolated zeros, norm equivalence, inverse/condition-number estimates, determinant/minor perturbation bounds, and stability of identifiable simultaneous diagonalization. Existing qualitative uniqueness machinery in `Causalean.Discovery.LinearDisentanglement` is the natural identification reference; the new result must be a neutral quantitative strengthening rather than a paper-specific restatement.

## Intended reuse
Reusable by robust covariance-based linear-disentanglement and BACKSHIFT-style identification results. The immediate consumer is a non-effective four-margin contraction theorem, but the substrate API must mention neither that paper nor confidence unions, corruption budgets, coverage statements, or finite-environment application wiring. It must work for generic finite real matrix families.

## May assume / must derive
May assume: finite dimension; a finite nonempty index family; explicit normalization; positive affine separation; explicit scale and condition bounds; compactness of the candidate set for the non-effective lemma; continuity and unique-zero/isolation hypotheses when stated abstractly.

Must derive: the quantitative residual-to-operator-distance estimate from these assumptions; all norm-conversion, matrix perturbation, and finite-family maximum/minimum steps used by the bound; positivity and attainment of the far-set residual minimum for the compactness lemma. Do not assume the desired Lipschitz bound, a prepackaged local inverse theorem whose conclusion is the target, or the positive far-family minimum itself.

## Non-goals (optional)
No confidence-region construction, real-closed-field quantifier elimination, effective root isolation, release-or-abstain procedure, corruption-aware algorithm, software implementation, finite-sample probability theorem, or paper-specific `*_Research` import. The compactness radius may remain existential/noncomputable; the local linear modulus must be explicit in its declared parameters.

## Known building blocks (optional)
Finite-dimensional real matrices; Frobenius/L2 and operator norms with comparison inequalities; transpose, determinant, invertibility and inverse-norm estimates; continuity of matrix operations and determinants; compactness and extreme-value results; finite sup/max bounds; and `Causalean.Discovery.LinearDisentanglement` for existing qualitative simultaneous-diagonalization uniqueness. Imports may use only Mathlib, Causalean, and neutral modules created within this study staging tree, never a CausalSmith paper module.


## Your tools
- Read the staging files and inspect the Causalean tree (root = the directory containing `Causalean.lean`; sources under `Causalean/`).
- Project search — run from `CausalSmith/tools`: `npm run search -- "<concepts>"` (find existing decls to reuse/dedup against), `npm run search -- --scope module "<concepts>"` (find the correct topical HOME file/area — use this for placement), `npm run search -- --type "<pattern>"` / `--goal "<goal>"`.
- lean-lsp for signatures / declaration files.

## What to decide
1. PLACEMENT — merge-first. Find the substrate's natural topical home with `--scope module`. STRONGLY prefer MERGING each decl into an existing `Causalean/.../X.lean`; only CREATE a new topic file inside the narrowest faithful existing top-level subject area. Never invent a generic holding area. Target ≤600 lines; split before ~900 only for an independent topic/proof chain.
2. NAMESPACE — rewrite every `CausalSmith.Substrate.QuantitativeSimultaneousCongruenceStability` reference to the chosen Causalean namespace (the namespace of the file it lands in).
3. REUSE / DEDUP — for each decl, search Causalean for one that already proves the SAME statement. If it exists, drop your reinvented version and use the existing one (add its import, point references at it). Reuse ONLY on genuine statement-equality — a rewire to a decl that merely looks similar will break the build. Dedup edits stay inside YOUR new content; never delete or alter an existing Causalean decl.
4. DOCUMENTATION (docstring-canonical) — every declaration that will render as a public library card gets a `/-- … -/` docstring whose FIRST paragraph is a self-contained natural-language translation for an econometrician with no Lean background (no Lean syntax, no field projections like `B.sigma` — say "the σ-algebra on B"; no "For every …" preamble restating the signature). This includes named local definitions or instances when the index extracts and displays them. `doc:gen` hard-fails if any published card would show “No natural-language translation yet.” Every new file opens with a `/-! … -/` module docstring stating what it provides. Theorem and lemma first paragraphs carry NL↔Lean CROSSLINKS: wrap the phrase translating each hypothesis or explicit binder in `[phrase](hyp:binderName)` (comma list `(hyp:h1,h2)` when one phrase covers several) and the conclusion phrase in `[phrase](goal)`, covering every binder and the conclusion; write the sentence to read naturally first, then bracket. `npm run lint:nl-links` is part of the integration gate and hard-fails on any incomplete or unannotated headline theorem.
5. HEADLINE + PAGE-DESCRIPTION curation — audit EVERY promoted Lean file and every newly created published namespace path before emitting the manifest. The documentation gate requires every file containing a public `theorem` or `lemma` to have at least one matching declaration in `headline_theorems` in the correct `doc/library_review/<Area>.json`. Curate MAIN results normally (identification theorem, estimand characterization, named decomposition, asymptotic linearity/normality/rate/optimality/efficiency result, sharp bound). If a theorem-bearing file contains only technical/supporting results, still choose its most representative reusable public theorem or lemma as that file's single required headline anchor; additional technical steps remain supporting-tier. Also give every NEW explorer page a short, reader-facing description: use the first paragraph of a roll-up module's `/-! ... -/` docstring when that module exists, otherwise add `namespace_intros["<path below Area>"]` to the area sidecar. Include intermediate directories created by a new subtree (for example, adding `Causalean.Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.PolynomialImageDimension.*` also requires a description for `AlgebraicGeometry`). Preserve every existing sidecar entry and stage the COMPLETE updated sidecar with a `write_file` op. Before output, cross-check the promoted file list and every new page path against the staged sidecar; never rely on a later failed `doc:gen` run to discover omissions.
6. API.md — for a NEW module, add a `<!-- GEN:Causalean.<Module> -->` / `<!-- /GEN -->` marker pair in `doc/API.md` where the per-decl table belongs (the system's `doc:gen` fills it — do NOT hand-write the table), plus any cross-cutting narrative for the new file.

## Output — WRITE bodies to staging, emit a TINY manifest
CRITICAL, read twice: do NOT put file contents inside the JSON. Large Lean bodies inside a JSON string are the #1 cause of a parse failure that aborts the whole integration (a truncated/mis-escaped string cannot be recovered). Instead:

1. WRITE every file body and every insert patch as a SEPARATE FILE under the staging directory:
   <repo-root>/CausalSmith/doc/study/quantitative-simultaneous-congruence-stability/coordinate_staging/round_1
   Use short names, e.g. `<repo-root>/CausalSmith/doc/study/quantitative-simultaneous-congruence-stability/coordinate_staging/round_1/foo.lean`, `<repo-root>/CausalSmith/doc/study/quantitative-simultaneous-congruence-stability/coordinate_staging/round_1/merge_x.lean`, `<repo-root>/CausalSmith/doc/study/quantitative-simultaneous-congruence-stability/coordinate_staging/round_1/area.json`. Put the EXACT bytes you want written/inserted into each staged file (namespaced, docstringed, ready to apply).
2. Emit ONLY a small JSON manifest that REFERENCES those staged files by `from` (relative to the staging dir). It contains no code — just short paths and one short anchor line per merge, so it always parses.

`{ "ops": [ … ], "notes": "<brief rationale>" }`. `target` paths are RELATIVE to the Causalean root. Op kinds:

- `{ "kind": "create_file", "target": "Causalean/…/Foo.lean", "from": "foo.lean", "newModule": "Causalean.….Foo" }` — write the staged `from` file as a NEW file at `target`. Set `newModule` (the Lean module name) ONLY for a new Lean module, so it is root-wired into `Causalean.lean`. Omit `newModule` for a new non-Lean record file.
- `{ "kind": "merge_lean", "target": "Causalean/…/X.lean", "anchor": "<a line already in X.lean>", "from": "merge_x.lean" }` — INSERT the staged `from` content after the first line containing `anchor` (empty anchor → append at end of file). INSERT-ONLY: the system preserves every existing byte and ROLLS BACK if a merge would change existing content. To add an import to an existing file, use a separate `merge_lean` anchored on an existing `import …` line (its `from` file holds just the import line). Multiple `merge_lean` ops may target the same file. If dependent inserts share one file/anchor, combine them into one staged file in dependency order, or anchor each later insert on text introduced by the prior one. Pick a SHORT, UNIQUE anchor line (a section header, a decl name) so it is unambiguous and easy to escape in JSON.
- `{ "kind": "write_file", "target": "doc/library_review/<Area>.json", "from": "area.json" }` — full-content write of a NON-Lean record file (headline sidecar, `doc/API.md`). Read the current file first, write the COMPLETE updated content to the staged `from` file (add entries/markers, never drop existing ones), and reference it here.

## Hard rules
- NEVER modify or delete an existing line in an existing Lean file. Integrating must be additive (new files + insert-only merges). If it genuinely requires editing an existing proven decl, do NOT — pick a different placement and explain in `notes`.
- Final Lean content may import and reference only Mathlib/Causalean modules. Rewrite every temporary staging reference; no `CausalSmith` import or qualified reference may remain in a staged create/merge body.
- Every `target` stays within the Causalean root; every `from` is a file you wrote under the staging dir.
- Do NOT run `lake build` / `library_index` / `embed` / `doc:gen` yourself — the system runs the full gate and rolls back on any failure. Emit only the manifest.
- Keep the manifest JSON small and valid: no code inside it, no trailing commas, all strings closed. If unsure, fewer ops with cleaner anchors.
